test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 21 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a race, an athlete covers a distance of 420 m in 140 sec in the first lap. He covers the second lap of the same distance in 70 sec. What is the average speed (in m/sec) of the athlete?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equal distances ⇒ Average speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y)

First speed = 420 ÷ 140 = 3 m/sec, Second speed = 420 ÷ 70 = 6 m/sec

Average speed = (2 × 3 × 6) ÷ (3 + 6)

= 36 ÷ 9 = 4 m/sec

**∴ Answer = 4 m/sec**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of each lap = 420 m; Time₁ = 140 sec; Time₂ = 70 sec

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 420 + 420 = 840 m

⇒ Total time = 140 + 70 = 210 sec

⇒ Average speed = 840 ÷ 210

⇒ = 4 m/sec

**∴ The correct answer is 4 m/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (General)

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Equal Distance Formula

If distances are equal: Avg speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y)

Unit Check

Speed = m/sec when distance in meters and time in seconds

Common Mistake

Do not take simple average of speeds unless time is equal
